newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan output rises, but uncertainties remain.
newsitem.headline: Japan output rises, but uncertainties remain.

text.p: Japan's economy is perking up, official data showed on Thursday, but lingering weakness in industrial output means the nation's central bank is likely to keep its loose grip on credit.
The Trade Ministry showed that industrial production, an engine of the economy, rose last month, helped by brisk output of automotive and telecommunications equipment.

But the good news on factory output was tempered by ministry forecasts of a dip in production over the next two months, a scenario which economists said would encourage policy makers to keep Japan's interest rates at a record low.
Industrial production is closely watched by financial markets for clues to the strength of Japan's tentative economic recovery, as well as changes in economic and monetary policy.

Industrial output rose 3.5 percent in October from the previous month in line with economists' predictions, which ranged from a rise of 2.5 percent to 4.1 percent. The ministry said it expected industrial output to drop 1.7 percent in November, and fall 0.2 percent in December.

"I think these numbers are just going to solidify the mentality that Japanese interest rates and certainly monetary policy aren't going to change any time soon," said Eric Nickerson, vice president at Capital Markets and Trading, Asia, Bank of America, Hong Kong.

The Bank of Japan has kept its key lending rate at a record low of 0.5 percent for just over a year to help haul the economy clear of the recession that followed the collapse of the 1980s "bubble" economy of inflated asset prices.

"Output forecasts dipping into the negative territory in November and in December underscored the prevailing market view that the Bank of Japan is likely to keep its easy policy on hold well into the next year," said Masayoshi Hasegawa, a manager at Norinchukin Bank.
The data triggered buying of Japanese government bonds. "The forecasts for the months ahead were considered weak, and slight buying ensued," said one trader at a trust bank.
The Trade Ministry said industrial production was on a gradual upward trend overall, despite the expected dips.
The data mirrored the findings of a central bank survey released on Wednesday which showed only a modest improvement in business confidence among Japanese manufacturers.
The quarterly corporate survey, known as the "tankan", showed that Japanese manufacturers remained cautious, given the uncertainty about the strength of the economic recovery.
Economists say a planned tax rise next year could dampen consumption and be a drag on the economy. The consumption tax will be raised from the current three percent to five percent from April 1.
That, along with a possible end to special income tax cuts implemented for the past two years to nurture the economic recovery, is expected to hamper growth.

Rising car exports helped to boost factory output in October. Japan's car exports rose a hefty 17.6 percent last month from a year earlier to 322,022 units, according to car industry data released on Thursday.
